top_choice_rationale: Buchwald and Hartwig's general ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a mature, widely used method with clean two-person attribution. It is chemically distinct from the 2010 C-C coupling prize (a different bottleneck, amido-palladium reductive elimination, solved by new ligand classes) and goes beyond Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide precursor. Targeted protein degradation (P002) is a stronger design principle but its consequences are mostly clinical-stage and a three-person cap cannot cover both the cereblon and VHL strands, so it ranks second. No award ranks last since a mature, well-attributed candidate exists.
